claim: Per-library React 19/RSC support, bundle sizes, and code-splitting for react-i18next, react-intl, Lingui, next-intl, Paraglide, typesafe-i18n in 2026.
quote: next-intl: Full, no `use client` required for server translations (~4KB client / 457B server-only). Paraglide: bundle sizes up to 70% smaller than equivalent runtime libraries.

claim: react-i18next hooks depend on React context so Server Components need the createInstance pattern; not a native App Router fit.
quote: Does react-i18next support react server components?

claim: RSC output is final HTML with no hydration step; server-resolved translations ship zero translation JS; next-intl assumes locale files in the repo; next-i18next is a shim for App Router.
quote: There's no hydration step for RSC output—the HTML is final... ship zero translation-related JavaScript to the client.

claim: next-intl uses awaitable getTranslations in async Server Components and useTranslations hook in Client Components via request-scoped config; Next.js-focused, no SPA docs.
quote: In case of async components, you can use the awaitable getTranslations function instead.

claim: Paraglide is a compiler-based i18n library emitting tree-shakable translations for up to 70% smaller bundles; repo star count.
quote: Compiler-based i18n library that emits tree-shakable translations, leading to up to 70% smaller bundle sizes.

claim: Paraglide ships 47-144 KB vs i18next 205-422 KB and stays flat as catalog grows because only used messages ship (tree-shaking).
quote: Paraglide's bundle remains constant at 47 KB... i18next's bundle expands from 205 KB to 414 KB—unused messages are tree-shaken away in Paraglide.

claim: Lingui uses identical Trans/useLingui in server and client; server useLingui reads a per-request I18n from React cache; requires SWC macro plugin and setI18n() in every page/layout.
quote: useLingui works as a simple function call which reads from the React cache... setI18n must be called in every page and layout, not just the root layout.

claim: Lingui repository, ~2 kb i18n runtime, star count.
quote: A readable, automated, and optimized (2 kb) internationalization for JavaScript

claim: FormatJS/react-intl repository and star count; most complete Intl/ICU support.
Vite natively supports dynamic import() locale-chunk splitting; react-intl passes loaded messages to IntlProvider; only the active locale ships initially.
quote: Vite supports dynamic import() natively... Your initial bundle only contains one locale... new locales are pulled on demand as separate chunks.

claim: typesafe-i18n is a lightweight (~1KB) codegen TypeScript i18n library; last major release 2023, largely single-maintainer; star count.
quote: A fully type-safe and lightweight internationalization library for all your TypeScript and JavaScript projects.

claim: react-i18next has mature, documented SSR support.
Real-world migration: ~40 KB i18next reduced to ~2 KB with Paraglide; only downside TypeScript type-checking lagging when adding many keys.
quote: 40KB just to handle translations... reduced to ~2KB with Paraglide.js. TypeScript type-checking can lag when rapidly adding multiple translations.

claim: react-intl is ~20KB gzipped, the heaviest option, overkill for simple key-value translations; with react-intl/react-i18next you manage catalog splitting and lazy loading manually.
quote: the largest library on this list (~20KB gzipped)... you typically manage catalog splitting and lazy loading manually.

claim: Server Components execute on the server and send only rendered output; no component JS shipped to the client.
quote: React Server Components... send only their rendered output to the browser — no component JavaScript is shipped to the client.

claim: Next.js App Router can run as a strict client-side SPA where everything renders client-side.
quote: Next.js can start as a static site or even a strict SPA where everything is rendered client-side.

claim: 2026 guide corroborating typesafe-i18n's smaller community and slower maintenance cadence versus react-i18next.
quote: The Definitive Guide to i18n Libraries for Next.js & React in 2026
